narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Abraham; steady and grave.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.note: The patriarch (Abram until 17:5), near a hundred years old; reverent, hospitable, bold yet humble in pleading.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.note: Abraham's wife (Sarai until 17:15), aged and barren; aggrieved in ch. 16, incredulous then afraid in ch. 18.

hagar.name: Hagar
hagar.note: Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, pregnant and fleeing; frightened, then awed.

angel.name: Angel
angel.note: The angel of the Lord at the well; the two angels at Sodom, urgent and commanding.

1.t: Now Sarai, the wife of Abram, had brought forth no children: but having a handmaid, an Egyptian, named Agar,

2.t: Behold, the Lord hath restrained me from bearing: go in unto my handmaid, it may be I may have children of her at least.
And when he agreed to her request,

3.t: She took Agar the Egyptian her handmaid, ten years after they first dwelt in the land of Chanaan, and gave her to her husband to wife.

4.t: And he went in to her. But she perceiving that she was with child, despised her mistress.

5.t: Thou dost unjustly with me: I gave my handmaid into thy bosom, and she perceiving herself to be with child, despiseth me. The Lord judge between me and thee.

6.t: And Abram made answer, and said to her:
Behold thy handmaid is in thy own hand, use her as it pleaseth thee.
And when Sarai afflicted her, she ran away.

7.t: And the angel of the Lord having found her, by a fountain of water in the wilderness, which is in the way to Sur in the desert,

8.t: Agar, handmaid of Sarai, whence comest thou? and whither goest thou?
I flee from the face of Sarai, my mistress.

9.t: And the angel of the Lord said to her:
Return to thy mistress, and humble thyself under her hand.

10.t: I will multiply thy seed exceedingly, and it shall not be numbered for multitude.

11.t: thou art with child, and thou shalt bring forth a son: and thou shalt call his name Ismael, because the Lord hath heard thy affliction.

12.t: He shall be a wild man: his hand will be against all men, and all men's hands against him: and he shall pitch his tents over against all his brethren.

13.t: And she called the name of the Lord that spoke unto her:
Thou the God who hast seen me.
13.q: the name she gives the Lord, read as her own address to him

13.t: Verily, here have I seen the hinder parts of him that seeth me.

14.t: Therefore she called that well, the well of him that liveth and seeth me. The same is between Cades and Barad.

15.t: And Agar brought forth a son to Abram: who called his name Ismael.

16.t: Abram was four score and six years old when Agar brought him forth Ismael.
